text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- B.C. to abolish welfare rule: Ottawa agrees to pay C$60 million for dropping of controversial residency requirement.
- Harris gives job loss new spin: Hospitals likened to Hula-Hoop fad.
- Quebec police probe data sales: Firms said to buy government files.
- Albanian unrest escalates: President rejects foreign mediation.
- John Major proposes switch to RRSP-style pensions: Tory plan would leave British poor with minimal benefits.
- Klein weaves a spell over Alberta: Charismatic guy-next-door Premier has become the embodiment of his province's values.
- Munk extends reach in Europe: Alliance with financier boosts TrizecHahn's real estate interests in Germany and Britian.
- Royal Bank voters reject activist's ideas: But Michaud allies claim victory in size of support for his governance proposals.
- Teamsters taking another run at a McDonald's outlet.
- New bid discussed for Altamira: Midland partner in talks, court told.
- Star choice attacks 'obstructive' BCE: Direct-to-home satellite-TV company also launches civil suit alleging BCE is abusing its dominant telecom market position.
- Activists lose as Royal Bank earnings soar.
